title: glTF 2.0 writer for typed-array meshes
purpose: Write typed-array meshes (positions, normals, uvs, vertex colours, indices) and a node hierarchy as a glTF 2.0 document with one embedded base64 buffer or as a GLB, with aligned buffer views, POSITION bounds and a metallic-roughness material per mesh. Use it to export procedural geometry without GLTFExporter.

engine.name: node
engine.notes: Pure JavaScript; also runs in browsers and workers. Output checked by loading it with three.js 0.186.1 GLTFLoader in headless Chrome.

exports.name: writeGltf
exports.summary: A glTF 2.0 document (JSON.stringify it for a .gltf file) with one base64 data URI buffer.

exports.name: writeGlb
exports.summary: The same scene as a GLB container.

exports.name: meshFromBufferGeometry
exports.summary: Copy a BufferGeometry's position, normal, uv, color and index into a writer mesh; refuses interleaved or normalized attributes.

exports.name: encodeBase64
exports.summary: RFC 4648 base64 with padding, written by hand.

exports.name: GLTF_WRITER_DEFAULTS
exports.summary: Frozen default options: generator and sceneName.

inputs.mesh: {positions: Float32Array xyz, normals?: Float32Array xyz, uvs?: Float32Array uv, colors?: Float32Array rgb or rgba, indices?: Uint8Array | Uint16Array | Uint32Array, name?, material?: {color: [r, g, b, a] linear, metallic, roughness, emissive: [r, g, b], doubleSided, name}}
inputs.node: {mesh?, translation?: [x, y, z], rotation?: unit quaternion [x, y, z, w], scale?: [x, y, z], children?: node indices, name?}

limits: Writes triangle lists only (mode 4), one primitive per mesh, one buffer, FLOAT attributes and unsigned indices: no textures, images, samplers, skins, morph targets, animations, cameras, lights, extensions or sparse or quantized accessors. Materials are plain metallic-roughness factors. Each mesh gets its own material even when two are equal. The data URI form grows the payload by a third over the binary; use writeGlb for large meshes. Only the Node 22 tests and three.js 0.186.1 GLTFLoader in headless Chrome on SwiftShader WebGL 2 were run.
technique_references: glTF 2.0 accessors, buffer views and buffers with 4-byte alignment
GLB container with a JSON and a BIN chunk
